items.headline: Man, 20, jailed nine years with caning for sexual offences against three girls
items.summary: A Singapore court sentenced a 20-year-old man to nine years’ jail and 12 strokes of the cane for sexual offences against three girls aged 13 and 14. Prosecutors noted he had given police statements over two earlier 2023 incidents but offended again in June 2024.

items.headline: Worker dies after being struck by a hose at a Jurong Port Road worksite
items.summary: A worker died after he was hit by a hose at a Jurong Port Road construction site, and the Ministry of Manpower said it is investigating the accident. It is the latest in a run of worksite fatalities the authorities have moved to curb.

items.headline: Two taken to hospital, 20 evacuated after fire in a Pasir Ris HDB flat
items.summary: The Singapore Civil Defence Force evacuated about 20 residents and took two people to hospital after a fire broke out in a bedroom of a Pasir Ris HDB flat. The blaze was put out and its cause is under investigation.

items.headline: Police probe interior design firm Axion Design over stalled home renovations
items.summary: Singapore police are investigating interior design firm Axion Design after customers complained of stalled renovations, unfinished work and missing furniture. Affected homeowners say they are out thousands of dollars in deposits.

items.headline: Crystal Jade shuts its Great World outlet in a third Singapore closure this year
items.summary: Homegrown chain Crystal Jade closed its Great World restaurant, its third Singapore closure in 2026, as mid-tier dining keeps feeling pressure from high rents and softer consumer spending.

items.headline: Fitch raises India’s FY26 growth forecast to 7.4% on GST-driven demand
items.summary: Fitch Ratings lifted India’s growth forecast for the current fiscal year to 7.4%, up from 6.9%, citing stronger consumer spending after the government’s GST 2.0 tax cuts. It expects easing inflation and rate cuts to support demand.

items.headline: India set to slip to the world’s sixth-largest economy as the rupee weakens
items.summary: India is projected to fall to the sixth-largest economy in 2026, with nominal GDP near $4.15 trillion, behind Britain and Japan, as an 11% rupee slide against the dollar shrinks output in dollar terms. Fitch expects the currency’s fall to be limited.

items.headline: China overtakes India as Bangladesh’s second-largest trading partner
items.summary: India has slipped behind China among Bangladesh’s top trading partners amid strained ties with Dhaka, underscoring Beijing’s deepening economic footprint in South Asia. The shift follows months of frosty India-Bangladesh relations.

items.headline: GST 2.0 cuts trim household costs by up to 13%, government says
items.summary: India’s revamped goods-and-services tax moved many essentials from 12% to 5% and several items from 28% to 18%, cutting household costs by as much as 13%. Ministers say the reform will lift consumption and add to GDP.

items.headline: Labour gathers in Liverpool as PM Burnham warns his party is ‘in peril’
items.summary: Thousands of Labour members convened in Liverpool for the party conference, where Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned the party is ‘in peril’ and must change direction. The gathering opens as his government faces pressure to define an economic plan.

items.headline: Reform UK vows to cut £80bn a year in spending as it targets Labour
items.summary: At its party conference, Reform UK’s Treasury spokesperson pledged to cut public spending by £80 billion a year by the end of the next parliament, as Reform and the Conservatives sharpen economic attacks on Andy Burnham’s government.

items.headline: UK borrowing costs hit a near-30-year high ahead of Burnham’s Budget
items.summary: The interest rate on 30-year UK government debt climbed to about 5.91%, a near-30-year high, as bond markets grew wary of Prime Minister Burnham’s plans to ramp up public spending before the autumn Budget.

items.headline: MPs debate a referendum on public ownership of England’s water sector
items.summary: In Westminster Hall, MPs debated an e-petition calling for a referendum on public ownership of England’s water sector, reflecting persistent anger over sewage spills and rising bills. The debate came as the Commons prepared to rise for conference recess.

items.headline: Russian drones strike near Poland’s border as Tusk warns of escalation
items.summary: Russian drones hit a petrol station and a train less than two kilometres from the Ukraine-Poland border, prompting Prime Minister Donald Tusk to say Poland cannot rule out attacks on its own territory. NATO chief Mark Rutte pledged more support for Kyiv.

items.headline: Trump and Xi set to meet at the White House on Sept 24
items.summary: President Donald Trump said he expects to discuss ‘almost everything’ with China’s Xi Jinping at a Sept 24 White House meeting, including trade, aircraft, the war in Ukraine, Gaza and AI. It would be their first summit of Trump’s new term.

items.headline: Oil holds above $100 as Iran ties reopening the Strait of Hormuz to sanctions relief
items.summary: Brent crude held above $100 a barrel with the Strait of Hormuz still effectively closed, as Iran’s foreign minister said an Oman-brokered deal to reopen the waterway hinges on sanctions relief and war reparations from Washington. Traffic through the strait has collapsed about 95%.

items.headline: Israel moves to strip citizenship of filmmakers over a prize-winning Gaza documentary
items.summary: Israel’s culture minister vowed to revoke the citizenship of filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor after their Gaza documentary won a Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival, drawing condemnation from Prime Minister Netanyahu. Rights groups called it an attack on free expression.

items.headline: Update: Sweden’s centre-left edges ahead as the count narrows to a single seat
items.summary: Sweden’s centre-left opposition led by Magdalena Andersson held a razor-thin edge — about 176 seats to 173 — over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s right-wing bloc as counting neared completion. Andersson said that if the result stands, ‘Sweden will get a new government’.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra with a focus on cybersecurity and computer use
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, a model it pitches for cybersecurity and agentic computer tasks, with a context window of roughly one million tokens. The launch lands amid a frenetic release pace across the leading AI labs.

items.headline: Anthropic lines up a record Nasdaq IPO as Nvidia weighs a $10bn stake
items.summary: AI developer Anthropic is preparing a Nasdaq listing targeting a valuation near $2 trillion — potentially the largest IPO on record — with chipmaker Nvidia in talks to anchor the offering with up to $10 billion. Both companies declined to comment on the still-preliminary plans.

items.headline: Meta reassigns thousands of staff into its consolidated AI unit
items.summary: Meta has moved roughly 7,000 employees into its consolidated AI organisation, part of a sweeping 2026 reshuffle as the company races rivals on frontier models. The shift shows how aggressively Big Tech is redeploying talent toward AI.

items.headline: AI leaders quietly work on an industry-led safety standards body
items.summary: Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind have held working-group meetings since July aimed at creating an industry-led standards organisation for AI, according to people familiar with the talks. The effort comes as regulators debate binding rules.

items.headline: Wall Street slips as the 10-year Treasury yield hits its highest since 2023
items.summary: US stocks fell on Monday as the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level since 2023, with investors bracing for the Federal Reserve’s rate decision. Higher energy costs from the Iran conflict have kept inflation pressure in focus.

items.headline: Fed poised to raise rates on Wednesday as inflation stays sticky
items.summary: Markets put the odds of a 25-basis-point Fed hike at Wednesday’s meeting above 80%, after hot August core CPI and a resilient labour market. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has said underlying inflation has not ‘meaningfully improved’.

items.headline: Baldwin Group agrees to a $7.7bn take-private deal
items.summary: Insurance brokerage The Baldwin Group agreed to be taken private by Sequence Holdings and DFO Management in a deal valued at about $7.7 billion, the latest in a busy run of 2026 dealmaking led by AI, healthcare and energy targets.

items.headline: Carlyle closes a $2.3bn infrastructure credit fund as private capital piles in
items.summary: Carlyle closed its second infrastructure credit fund at about $2.3 billion, part of a wave of private-capital fundraising in 2026 as investors chase energy and digital-infrastructure lending. Dealmaking has been led by AI, healthcare and energy.

items.headline: 🏎️ Hamilton concedes the title fight, says ‘there’s no stopping’ Antonelli
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton appeared to give up his 2026 title bid, saying ‘there’s no stopping’ Kimi Antonelli after the Italian won in Madrid to stretch his lead. Antonelli tops the standings on 292 points, 81 clear of George Russell.

items.headline: 🏎️ F1 heads to Baku with Antonelli’s title all but decided
items.summary: The championship moves to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, run on Saturday, Sept 26 to avoid Baku’s Remembrance Day. Lando Norris trails Antonelli by 83 points and must win to keep even a slim mathematical hope alive.

items.headline: 🏏 India win an eighth Women’s Asia Cup, beating Sri Lanka by 72 runs
items.summary: India lifted a record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title, beating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Dubai final. Shafali Verma (68) and Smriti Mandhana (59) put on a 129-run opening stand before Sree Charani took 4/20.

items.headline: 🎾 Davis Cup Final 8 opens this week with Sinner and Alcaraz set to star
items.summary: The Davis Cup Finals group stage gets under way in the coming days, with Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz among the marquee names as eight nations chase the title. It is the first big team event of the post-US Open stretch.

items.headline: Aging ‘zombie’ cells hijack faulty mitochondria to fuel chronic inflammation
items.summary: Researchers found that senescent ‘zombie’ cells use malfunctioning mitochondria to switch on inflammatory genes, keeping the immune system in a prolonged state of alert. The work points to new targets for age-related inflammation.

items.headline: Alzheimer’s disrupts the 3D folding of DNA inside brain cells, study finds
items.summary: A new study shows the three-dimensional organisation of DNA is disrupted across several brain-cell types in Alzheimer’s disease, altering how key genes are switched on and off. The finding could reshape how the disease is understood.

items.headline: Scientists watch two DNA strands pair up despite their mutual repulsion
items.summary: Researchers directly observed how two negatively charged DNA molecules can pair, with positively charged metal ions appearing to bridge the gap between them. The observation clarifies a long-standing puzzle in molecular biology.

items.headline: A new twist on the Hall effect overturns a century-old assumption
items.summary: Carnegie Mellon researchers reported an unexpected form of the Hall effect, upending the long-held assumption that the electrical response appears only when a magnetic field is perpendicular to a material. It could aid the design of new electronic devices.

items.headline: AI scan of 400,000 posts surfaces under-reported side effects of GLP-1 drugs
items.summary: An AI analysis of about 400,000 online posts from users of drugs such as Ozempic and Mounjaro flagged symptoms rarely captured in trials, including menstrual changes, chills and fatigue. Researchers say patient forums may reveal overlooked effects.

fun_fact.headline: Gallium melts in your hand at below body temperature
fun_fact.body: Gallium is a metal that melts in your hand: it turns to a silvery liquid at just 29.8°C (85.6°F), below body temperature. Yet it stays liquid over an enormous range — it does not boil until about 2,200°C — one of the longest liquid ranges of any element. Unlike mercury it is non-toxic to handle, and it is a key ingredient in LEDs and smartphone chips.

puzzle.title: The Lone Truth
puzzle.body:
A sheet lists ten numbered statements:

Statement 1: ‘Exactly one statement on this sheet is false.’
Statement 2: ‘Exactly two statements on this sheet are false.’
Statement 3: ‘Exactly three statements on this sheet are false.’
… and so on, down to …
Statement 10: ‘Exactly ten statements on this sheet are false.’

Exactly one of the ten statements is true. Which one is it?
puzzle.approach: The ten statements contradict one another — work out how many can be true at once.
puzzle.answer:
Statement 9.

Each statement claims a different number of false statements, so no two can be true at once — at most one is true. We are told exactly one is true, which means exactly nine are false. The statement asserting ‘exactly nine are false’ is Statement 9, so Statement 9 is the true one, and it is consistent with every other statement being false.

word_puzzle.title: Say It Another Way
word_puzzle.body:
Rearrange all the letters of each phrase to reveal the answer:

1. DIRTY ROOM  →  a 9-letter place people sleep
2. THE CLASSROOM  →  a 12-letter person in charge of it
3. ELEVEN PLUS TWO  →  a phrase worth the same, built from the very same letters
word_puzzle.approach: Each phrase uses exactly the same letters as its answer — rearrange every letter, none added or dropped.
word_puzzle.answer:
1. DIRTY ROOM = DORMITORY
2. THE CLASSROOM = SCHOOLMASTER
3. ELEVEN PLUS TWO = TWELVE PLUS ONE  (both equal 13 — and both use the identical 13 letters)
